title: Live Preview: start scene/frame override is ignored (scene override no-ops at runtime)
description:
USER REPORT
-----------
In Live Preview, overriding the start SCENE (and to a lesser extent the start FRAME) does
not change the previewed SWF as expected — the override appears ignored; the preview plays
from the default start. Reproduces when picking a non-default scene in the
"Scene"/"Frame" controls of the Live Preview control bar.

INVESTIGATION (CODE-only; no Ruffle/e2e run — port held by another agent)
HEAD at investigation: d1fe81cb36bd79d93d07f29eba684cce60a72228

Traced path end-to-end:
  LivePreviewPanel control (preview-start-scene / preview-start-frame selects)
    -> onPrefsChange -> Shell setPreviewPrefs (re-renders prefs)            [OK]
    -> startAt memo {sceneIndex: prefs.startScene, frame: prefs.startFrame} [OK]
    -> useLivePreview startKey effect -> controllerRef.request()            [OK, recompiles]
    -> controller.compileFn -> applyStartAt(liveDoc, startAt)               [OK]
    -> compileDocToBytes(derived, {skipSystemFontPrompt:true})              [OK, uses targetDoc]
    -> RufflePlayer reloads on new swfBytes identity                        [OK]

JOB 2 (empirical, unit-level): compiled the SAME doc WITH vs WITHOUT the override via
compileDocument and compared bytes. They DIFFER in both cases:
  - frame override (single scene, start frame 10): 64 -> 84 bytes (differ)
  - scene override (start scene 2 / frame 3):       66 -> 98 bytes (differ)
So startAt + the compile path DO emit something different. The React wiring, the
controller recompile trigger, applyStartAt's shallow-clone + gotoAndPlay prepend, and
compileDocToBytes(targetDoc) are all CORRECT. Rules out gaps (a) override-not-wired,
(b) startAt-not-applied / wrong doc compiled.

PRECISE GAP = (c) WRONG TARGET — the scene-name gotoAndPlay form is unsupported by the
AS2 compiler, so the emitted goto cannot reach the target scene/frame.

startAt.ts buildStartScript() emits, for a later scene:
  gotoAndPlay("Level Two", 3);                      (startAt.ts:50-51)
i.e. the TWO-ARGUMENT scene-name form (arg0 = scene name string, arg1 = frame).

But the AS2 compiler builtin handles ONLY the single-argument numeric form:
  packages/core/src/as2/compiler.ts:2326-2332 (gotoAndPlay)
  packages/core/src/as2/compiler.ts:2335-2341 (gotoAndStop)
It compiles ONLY expr.args[0], pushes it, and emits ActionGotoFrame2 (0x9F) with
flags=0x01 (PlayFlag=1, SceneBiasFlag=0). The SECOND argument (the frame) is DROPPED
entirely, and there is no scene-name handling at all.

Bytecode evidence (compileAS2 output, hex):
  gotoAndPlay(10):              96 05 00 07 0a000000  9f 01 00 01  ...   (correct: pushes 10)
  gotoAndPlay("Level Two", 3):  88 0c 00 01 00 "Level Two" 00  96 02 00 08 00  9f 01 00 01  ...
      -> pushes ONLY the string "Level Two"; frame 3 never pushed; GotoFrame2 flags=0x01.

Runtime semantics (ruffle/core/src/avm1/activation.rs:1374-1389 action_goto_frame_2):
GotoFrame2 pops ONE value and calls movie_clip::goto_frame with scene_offset=0. A string
operand is resolved as a FRAME LABEL (frame_label_to_number). A scene NAME is NOT a frame
label (scenes are emitted in SceneAndFrameLabelData tag 86 via scenelabels.ts, not as
frame labels), so "Level Two" resolves to nothing and the goto NO-OPS (stays at frame 1).
The frame arg (3) is lost too. => the SCENE override is silently ignored at runtime even
though the SWF bytes differ. (The single-scene numeric FRAME override, gotoAndPlay(10),
compiles correctly and DOES work — consistent with the user noticing scene override as the
worst case.)

So the report's "preview unchanged" is gap (c): startAt's gotoAndPlay targets a scene by
NAME, but the compiler emits a frame-label GotoFrame2 that cannot resolve a scene name and
drops the frame argument.

MINOR (not the bug): useLivePreview.ts:119 comment says the start-change recompile is
"immediate, no debounce" but line 126 calls request() WITHOUT {immediate:true}, so it is
debounced (~350ms). Functionally fine, just a latency/comment mismatch — optionally also
pass {immediate:true} there for snappy re-seek.

FIX DIRECTION
-------------
The override IS wired and DOES recompile; the only defect is the scene-name goto target.
Options (any one closes the user-visible bug):
  1. Teach the AS2 compiler the multi-arg scene form: gotoAndPlay(sceneName, frame) /
     gotoAndStop(sceneName, frame). To jump to scene S frame F, the correct AVM1 is to
     resolve the scene's ABSOLUTE start frame (scene start offset + (F-1)) and emit a
     GotoFrame2 with that absolute frame number — OR set SceneBiasFlag and push the scene
     bias. Simplest robust approach for the compiler: keep single-operand GotoFrame2 but
     make startAt compute the ABSOLUTE frame.
  2. PREFERRED (compiler-free): change startAt.ts buildStartScript to emit an ABSOLUTE
     frame number for later scenes instead of the scene-name form. Compute the cumulative
     frame offset of sceneIndex across preceding scenes (sum of sceneFrameCount(doc, i) for
     i < sceneIndex) + (frame) and emit gotoAndPlay(absFrame) / gotoAndStop(absFrame).
     Because the main timeline is the concatenation of all scenes (see scenelabels.ts scene
     frame offsets and the frame loop concatenating scenes), an absolute frame number lands
     in the right scene+frame and needs NO compiler change. Verify the offset matches the
     compiler's scene concatenation order.
  3. If keeping the scene-name string form, the compiler must (a) NOT drop arg1, (b) emit a
     GotoFrame2 that resolves the scene, which requires the scene-name path Ruffle supports
     (scene resolution is via SceneAndFrameLabelData) — more involved than option 2.

VERIFICATION
------------
- Unit: extend packages/authoring-ui/src/__tests__/livePreviewStartAt.test.ts with a
  multi-scene case; compile via compileDocument and assert the emitted DoAction GotoFrame2
  targets the correct ABSOLUTE frame (decode the goto operand) — and that with vs without
  the override the goto lands in the target scene.
- AS2 compiler unit: if option 1/3, add gotoAndPlay/gotoAndStop multi-arg coverage in the
  core as2 compiler tests.
- E2E (when port 1420 frees): a Ruffle oracle that sets start scene=2/frame=N in the Live
  Preview control bar and asserts the rendered first frame matches scene 2 / frame N (not
  scene 1 / frame 1). Per CLAUDE.md Verification: byte tests are necessary but Ruffle is
  the acceptance truth for any goto/seek behavior.

KEY FILES
---------
- packages/authoring-ui/src/preview/startAt.ts:33-52 (buildStartScript; scene-name form)
- packages/core/src/as2/compiler.ts:2325-2341 (gotoAndPlay/gotoAndStop builtins; single
  numeric arg only, drops 2nd arg, no scene-name support)
- packages/authoring-ui/src/preview/useLivePreview.ts:119-127 (start-change recompile;
  also the debounce/comment mismatch)
- packages/swf/src/scenelabels.ts (scene boundaries -> SceneAndFrameLabelData tag 86; basis
  for computing absolute scene start frames in option 2)
- ruffle/core/src/avm1/activation.rs:1374-1389 (action_goto_frame_2 runtime semantics)

ROOT CAUSE (one line): Live Preview's start-scene override emits gotoAndPlay("SceneName",
frame), but the AS2 compiler only supports gotoAndPlay(frameNumber) — it pushes the scene
NAME as a frame label and drops the frame arg, so GotoFrame2 finds no matching label and
no-ops; fix by emitting an absolute frame number from startAt (preferred) or adding
multi-arg/scene-name support to the compiler.
